transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place, and I really appreciate your time. Um, I guess what brings me in is... well, I've been having a little trouble keeping my mind on tasks lately. It's probably nothing major, just normal aging maybe, but I can't seem to stay focused long enough to finish things, even when they're really important for work. Like, I do computer support, and I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and... well, ten minutes later I'll realize I've just reread the same log entries three times and I still don't know what they say. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, doctor, not really. I mean, I don't think so? I generally try to stay pretty positive. I definitely haven't lost interest in my hobbies or anything like that—I still really enjoy my time off. 

I wouldn't say I feel sad... mostly just, well, a little frustrated with myself for messing up at work with the focus stuff I mentioned. But definitely not down in the dumps. I hope that answers your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory, like forgetting things more often than usual, or trouble finding the right words when you're speaking?

Well, my vocabulary is fine, I think. I don't really struggle to find words. But as for forgetting things... I mean, everyone forgets a little bit, right? I am 53, so maybe it's just normal wear and tear. 

But, um... I guess I do have some slip-ups. It's a bit embarrassing to admit. I'll forget ordinary things, but they end up being kind of important. Like, I'll forget to return a client's call, or... or I'll completely miss paying the cloud backup bill for work. Or if I'm heading to this volunteer class I teach, I'll show up and realize I didn't bring the right display adapter. 

It's just silly mistakes, mostly, but then I end up spending the whole next day apologizing to everyone and trying to patch up the damage. I feel awful when I let people down like that. I really try my best to keep on top of it. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... does that answer what you were asking about?
Have you been experiencing any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping more than usual?

Oh, no, not at all. My sleep has been pretty normal, thankfully. I usually don't have any trouble drifting off, and I definitely don't sleep the day away or anything like that. 

I always try to make sure I get a good night's rest so I can be as helpful as possible for my clients the next morning. I mean, I might toss and turn once in a blue moon, just like anyone, but nothing that seems like a real problem or a big change. I usually get a standard seven or eight hours. 

Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Have you been having trouble organizing tasks or finishing things once you start them, even if they’re simple or familiar?

Well, um... I guess I might have a little bit of trouble with that lately. It's not that I don't want to finish things, I really do try to get everything done perfectly. It's just... well, at work, we recently lost our old ticketing system and the escalation calendar we used to use. I didn't realize how much I leaned on them until they were gone. 

Now, I don't know, things just get a little messy? My desk ends up covered in these piles of sticky notes, and I'll have half-finished emails open, and reminders for the chess club I help out with mixed in with parts orders for clients... I try to keep it neat, I really do. But honestly, sometimes I just can't figure out what needs to happen first. It all sort of blurs together until, well, until something is already overdue and I'm scrambling to fix it. 

I feel terrible when it happens. I know I should be better at managing it on my own. I hope I'm not making myself sound completely incompetent... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you noticed any decrease in your ability to feel pleasure or satisfaction from activities that you usually enjoy?

No, no, I wouldn't say that. I still really enjoy the things I've always liked. I mean, I still look forward to helping out with the chess club, and I genuinely like fixing things for my clients. 

I guess sometimes I might get a little distracted or overwhelmed with the mess on my desk, like I mentioned, but it's not because I don't care or don't find satisfaction in my work or hobbies. I still get a lot of joy out of being useful and doing a good job. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude about everything. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Have you been feeling guilty or blaming yourself more than usual, even when things aren’t really your fault?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I feel guilty about things that aren't my fault. I mean, I definitely take responsibility for my own mistakes—like when I mess up the scheduling or lose track of a client's ticket, like I was saying before. I do feel bad about those things, because I know I should be doing better. 

But I don't just sit around blaming myself for everything under the sun, you know? I try to be really fair about it. If it's my mess, I own it and try to fix it so no one else is inconvenienced. I just want to be a reliable person for the people who count on me. 

Is that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm feeling.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, have you been more restless or fidgety lately?

Well, I definitely wouldn't say I'm moving slowly. I've always had a lot of energy, which I think is a good thing, right? It helps me get through the day. 

But, um... I guess maybe I have been a little bit... restless? It's really nothing major, just sort of nervous energy, I suppose. Like, if I'm sitting with a client trying to troubleshoot their network, or if we're in a longer chess club meeting... I might not even realize I'm doing it at first, but my leg will just be bouncing under the table. Or I'll find myself clicking my pen over and over, or just twisting a little plastic cable tie around in my fingers. 

I try really hard to keep it under control because I don't want to bother anyone, but sometimes I don't notice until somebody finally gives me that look, you know? And then I stop immediately, of course. I really don't mean to be disruptive. I just... I guess sitting perfectly still has been a little tricky lately. Does that sound like what you're asking about? I hope that's an okay answer.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your thinking, like confusion, trouble making decisions, or difficulty recognizing familiar people or places?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, my memory for people and places is perfectly fine. I'd never forget a client's face or anything like that. And I'm definitely not confused about where I am or what's going on. 

I guess... well, like I said before, sometimes my desk gets a bit messy and I might get a little overwhelmed figuring out which ticket to tackle first, but that's just because I want to make sure I'm prioritizing the right people, you know? It's not like I can't make a decision at all. I just want to make the *best* decision so I don't let anyone down. 

But as far as real confusion or forgetting familiar things? No, absolutely not. My mind is still sharp. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.

Have you found yourself acting impulsively or doing things without thinking them through lately, like interrupting others, making hasty decisions, or feeling like you just can't sit still even when you need to?

Well, I try really hard not to be impulsive in a bad way. I always want to be thoughtful and professional. But, um... I guess maybe sometimes, especially in tech discussions at work, I can get a little... overeager? 

Like, a client will be explaining an issue they're having, and the answer just immediately jumps into my head. And... well, sometimes I end up cutting people off. Even when I know better. I might start talking over them, or I'll just sort of reach out and grab the keyboard before they've even finished explaining the problem to me. 

I feel awful when I realize I've done it, because I really don't mean to be rude or interrupt them. I just get so focused on wanting to fix it for them right then and there so they can get back to their day, you know? I'm really trying to be better about waiting until they're completely done speaking. 

Does... does that answer what you were asking? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible listener or anything. I really do care about what they're saying.
Have these difficulties with focus, organization, and restlessness been causing you significant distress or affecting your ability to perform well at work or in other important areas of your life?

Well, I... I don't want to make it sound like everything is falling apart, because it's not. I'm still working hard and trying my best. But... I suppose it has been a little tough lately. 

Since I lost the structure of my old job, things have just been... trickier to manage. I hate to admit it, but my reputation has taken a bit of a hit. I've actually lost a few freelance clients recently. And, um, there was a senior service-manager role that I was really hoping for, but I missed out on it. I think... well, I think people might be starting to feel like they can't trust me to follow through on things, even though I really do want to. 

It's just been a bit stressful for my wife and me, worrying about money because of all this. I feel terrible about it, honestly. I'm really trying to get back on track so I don't let anyone else down. I hope that makes sense? I know it's not the most positive update, but I want to be honest with you so we can figure this out.

Looking back at your childhood, did you have a lot of difficulty staying focused, sitting still, or following through on tasks, even when you wanted to? For example, did you struggle in school with attention or often act impulsively?

Well, um... I guess if I really think back to when I was a kid... maybe a little bit? I mean, I was a good kid, I promise. I wasn't trying to be disruptive or anything. I just... I had a lot of energy. 

Actually, my mom still jokes about it sometimes. She says that back in grade school, my report cards would always say I was a bright student. But... well, they also usually mentioned that I had a hard time staying in my seat. And, um, I guess I had a habit of blurting out answers before the teacher called on me. Kind of like what I was saying about work earlier, just getting a little too eager to help. 

Oh, and the homework thing... I would actually do my homework, I swear I did! But somehow I'd manage to lose it between my house and the classroom. It was so frustrating because I really wanted to show the teacher I'd done the work. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker. I really did want to do well and be a good student. Does that... is that the kind of thing you're looking for about my childhood?
Were you experiencing difficulties with focus, restlessness, or impulsivity before you turned 12 years old?

Yes, I, um... I think so. Like I was just saying, my mom still tells those stories about my old report cards from grade school. So that would have been well before I turned 12. 

I really hope it doesn't sound like I was a bad kid or anything. I was just... enthusiastic, I guess? The teachers always said I was bright, which was nice of them. But, yeah, they did mention the whole not staying in my seat thing, and blurting out the answers, and... losing the homework that I really, truly had finished. 

So, yes, I suppose those things were happening back then. Does that... does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.

Yes, I, um... I think so. Like I was just saying, my mom still tells those stories about my old report cards from grade school. So that would have been well before I turned 12. 

I really hope it doesn't sound like I was a bad kid or anything. I was just... enthusiastic, I guess? The teachers always said I was bright, which was nice of them. But, yeah, they did mention the whole not staying in my seat thing, and blurting out the answers, and... losing the homework that I really, truly had finished. 

So, yes, I suppose those things were happening back then. Does that... does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.

inference.note: The patient reported a history of inattention, restlessness, and impulsivity beginning before age 12, which persisted into adulthood and are now causing significant impairment in occupational functioning. This presentation is most consistent with F90.0 (Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive type). The other candidates (F33.0, F06.7) are less likely given the absence of depressive symptoms and no evidence of organic mental disorder.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking help
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a long-standing pattern of inattention, impulsivity, and restlessness beginning before age 12 and persisting into adulthood, consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. There is no evidence of major depressive episode or psychotic disorder.
